title: Giant mechs, tech demos, pixel art and the end of the world… my first experiments
author: john068
selftext:
I've been playing around with Codex (Sol and Astra), with some additional refinement here and there using Opus 5.5. Mostly working with Three.js, trying out different genres and seeing what I can build.

Here's what I've made so far, my first experiments:

**Tokyo Impact**: A pretty simple giant mecha fighting game using Three.js and Rapier for physics. It was really just an excuse to create some destructible buildings and see how they collapse. I ended up adding a few different modes, including one where you're just a civilian working in a call center trying to survive the chaos. It’s a pretty pointless game but it was just a 2-day project.

**Tech Demos Factory**: A collection of 10 real-time 3D tech demos (inspired by 3DMark and old-school PC demos). Again, built with three.js and mostly an excuse to mess around with cool-looking environments (some more than others). It gives you a GPU score, and I also added a rail shooter mode where you can unlock a hidden scenario. It's also somehow connected to the next "game".

**Mishi's Pixel Escapades**: A super simple hidden-object game where you try to find a cat and other objects hidden in several scenarios. Made with javascript and HTML5. It has 15 simple animated pixel art scenes (mostly to test AI pixel art skills) and relaxing, procedurally generated music. You can also unlock two extra scenarios, one of them by playing Tech Demos Factory.

**BRK/EARTH**: A geopolitical apocalypse "simulator" that I started a few months ago. It went from something very serious and complex to something completely chaotic and stupid, more like a dark-humour satire about the end of the world. Built with three.js again, with a low-poly style. There's also a cloudflare endpoint with an agent that analyzes real-world news and adjusts relationships between countries. But things get out of hand pretty quickly… it's basically about how many minutes you can survive before a cataclysm ends the world. Originally, I used Gemini nano to process the in-game news feed and make the events a bit more coherent, but it was painfully slow and didn't work that well. So I ended up replacing it with a system that generates situations from thousands of possible combinations. It's much faster, although half the time the events make absolutely no sense… like the game itself.

They're all free to play in the browser:

[https://mamuuutgames.itch.io/](https://mamuuutgames.itch.io/)
